title: Machine-learning guided discovery of emergent antimicrobial activity from dynamic covalent assemblies（2b-RAD-M）
author: Yuanfeng Li
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Define sample groups
steps.instruction: Collect a total of 18 oral samples from the Streptococcus mutans‑induced rat caries model and assign them to three groups (n = 6 per group): the A5B5 treatment group (A5B5‑1 to A5B5‑6), the PBS‑treated caries control group (Caries‑1 to Caries‑6), and the chlorhexidine (CHX)‑treated positive control group (CHX‑1 to CHX‑6).

steps.title: Prepare 2bRAD‑M libraries
steps.instruction: Send the 18 samples to OE Biotech (Qingdao, China) for library preparation using a Type IIB restriction enzyme‑based 2bRAD‑M workflow.

substeps.instruction: Digest DNA with the Type IIB restriction enzyme BcgI.
Ligate adapters to the digested fragments.
Amplify the adapter‑ligated fragments by PCR.
Add barcode indexes to each library.

steps.title: Sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Sequence the indexed libraries on an Illumina NovaSeq PE150 platform.

steps.title: Analyze 2bRAD tags
steps.instruction: Perform downstream bioinformatic analysis: quality‑control the 2bRAD tags, map them to a species‑resolved 2bRAD marker database built from GTDB and Ensembl microbial genomes, filter candidate taxa using a Gscore threshold greater than 5, and compute species‑level relative abundances from mapped reads and species‑specific marker counts according to published 2bRAD‑M protocols.
